title: WHAT DO I HAVE VS. WHAT DO I NEED?
content:
If you want to make money online, it can feel like you have a thousand decisions to make before you can even start. You don't. Underneath all of the business models, platforms, products, and advice, there are two basic problems to solve.

First, you need something to sell. Second, you need a way to sell it.

Those are different problems. This library is here to help you solve the first one.

Knowing that you want to "make money online" is a goal, but it doesn't tell you what someone will pay you for. Even "I want to sell digital products" is still a direction rather than a specific answer. On the other hand, "I want to create a one-off digital guide for first-time dog owners" is specific enough that your next questions can be about that particular idea.

You don't need every detail figured out before you leave this library. You just need a direction that is specific enough to investigate.

WHAT COUNTS AS KNOWING WHAT YOU'RE SELLING?
You do not need a product name, final price, supplier, website, or finished offer yet. The question is whether you know what kind of value a customer would actually be paying you for.

"I want to work for myself," "I want passive income," and "I want to sell digital products" can describe what you want, but they still leave the thing being sold undecided. A direction becomes useful when it is concrete enough to investigate. "A one-off digital guide for first-time dog owners" gives you something specific to ask questions about.

HOW TO USE THIS LIBRARY
Do not assume you are supposed to read PDF 01 through PDF 46. Each guide answers one question and points toward the next relevant one. Skip branches that clearly do not fit, and go back when a choice stops fitting. The goal is not to learn every business model. It is to find one direction worth investigating.

DECISION CHECK
You are ready to leave this library only when you can finish a sentence like, "I want to sell ______ to ______." It can still contain assumptions that need research. If the blank is still "something online," "digital products," "stuff I make," or another broad category, keep going.

EXAMPLE
Broad: "I want an online business."
Closer: "I want to sell a service."
Useful direction: "I want to provide monthly remote bookkeeping for small home-service businesses."

The last version gives you something concrete to investigate without pretending the entire business is already figured out.

I DON'T KNOW WHAT I SHOULD SELL.
You're in the right place. You won't need to read every PDF in this library. You'll follow the questions that apply to you, explore the options that interest you, and skip the ones that don't.

NEXT → PDF 02: WHAT CAN I SELL?

I ALREADY KNOW EXACTLY WHAT I WANT TO SELL.
Then you've already solved the problem this library was designed to solve. Your next major question is how you're going to sell it, which belongs in the separate HOW DO I SELL IT? system.

One step at a time. You'll get there.

BEFORE YOU MOVE ON
You are not trying to prove that your idea will work yet. You are deciding what idea deserves that investigation. There is a big difference between choosing a direction and making an unsupported claim that the direction is viable.

That means it is completely acceptable to finish this library with a sentence that includes, "I want to investigate..." rather than, "I know this will succeed."

WHAT "KNOWING WHAT TO SELL" ACTUALLY MEANS

You do not need a finished product, supplier, price, brand name, or business plan before you can say you know what you want to sell.

You do need more than a category.

"I want to sell physical products" tells you where to keep exploring. It does not yet tell you what business you are considering.

"I want to create my own branded protein powder through a contract manufacturer for women who struggle to consume enough protein" is different. There are still major questions to answer, but those questions are now about a particular business direction: the customer, product requirements, manufacturing options, costs, regulations, demand, and viability.

That is the threshold this library is trying to reach.

Think of it as changing the kind of uncertainty you have. At the beginning, the uncertainty is, "What kind of business could I even start?" At the end, it should sound more like, "I know which business I want to investigate, and here are the specific things I still need to learn."

That is enough to move forward.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If you still need to decide what you are selling, go to PDF 02. If you can already describe the specific thing, customer, and basic way the sale creates income, do not keep exploring just because more PDFs exist. Your next major problem belongs to HOW DO I SELL IT?
